content: Larva migrans refers to a group of conditions caused by the migration of nematode larvae through human tissues. These conditions are classified based on the affected area of the body: 1. Cutaneous larva migrans: This is a dermatological condition caused by the larvae of various nematode parasites. It manifests as serpiginous, erythematous, and pruritic tracks on the skin, typically resulting from the larvae burrowing through the epidermis. 2. Visceral larva migrans: This condition occurs primarily in children and is caused by the migration of nematode larvae through internal organs such as the liver, lungs, and sometimes the central nervous system. It can lead to systemic symptoms such as fever, hepatomegaly, and eosinophilia. 3. Ocular larva migrans: This is an ocular manifestation of larva migrans syndrome, where the larvae invade the eye. It can result in visual disturbances, retinal damage, and in severe cases, blindness. 4. Larva migrans profundus (Gnathostomiasis): This is a deeper tissue infection caused by the larvae of the nematode Gnathostoma. It can lead to subcutaneous swelling, pain, and in some cases, systemic complications. Diagnosis through Physical Examination: Skin Examination: In cases of cutaneous larva migrans, the physical examination reveals characteristic serpiginous, raised, and erythematous tracks on the skin. These tracks are often intensely pruritic and may migrate over time. Genitalia Examination: Although not commonly involved, larva migrans lesions may occasionally be observed in the genital region. These lesions would present similarly to those on other parts of the skin, with serpiginous tracks and associated pruritus.
